Question ID: STAT_U02_L06_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.5

In a normal model, about what percent of values are within two standard deviations of the mean?

feedback.text: The empirical rule gives about 95% within two standard deviations.
About 68% is within one standard deviation.
Half the data is not the empirical-rule estimate for two standard deviations.
About 99.7% is within three standard deviations.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U02_L06_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.6

A normal model has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. What interval contains about 68% of values?

feedback.text: This is two standard deviations from the mean.
This only includes values above the mean.
About 68% are within one standard deviation: 100 - 15 to 100 + 15.
This is three standard deviations from the mean.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U02_L06_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.5

A normal model has mean 60 and standard deviation 8. About what percent is above 68?

feedback.text: About 34% lies between the mean and one standard deviation above.
68 is one standard deviation above the mean, so about 16% is above it.
68% is within one standard deviation, not above one standard deviation.
About 84% is below one standard deviation above the mean.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U02_L06_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.6

A test score distribution is normal with mean 70 and standard deviation 5. About what percent is between 65 and 75?

feedback.text: 65 to 75 is one standard deviation below and above the mean.
About 95% would be within two standard deviations.
About 34% is only one side from the mean to one standard deviation.
About 16% is one tail beyond one standard deviation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U02_L06_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DVD.5

What does estimating a population percentage from a normal model require first?

answer.text: The data must be categorical only

feedback.text: Normal models are for numerical distributions.

answer.text: The standard deviation must be zero

feedback.text: A standard deviation of zero would mean no spread and is not a typical normal model.

answer.text: The distribution must have two separate peaks

feedback.text: Two peaks suggest a normal model may not be appropriate.

answer.text: The data should be reasonably fit by a normal model

feedback.text: Population percentage estimates rely on the model being appropriate.
